title: Beyond the 956: Henry Garner Jr., founding Rose Royce drummer, dies at 72
excerpt: Henry Garner Jr., a founding member and the longtime drummer of the legendary soul and funk group Rose Royce, has died at 72. The group announced his passing on November 25, 2026.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Henry Garner Jr., a founding member and the longtime drummer of the legendary soul and funk group Rose Royce, has died at 72.

Rose Royce announced Garner's death on Tuesday, November 25, 2026, writing on social media: “It is with great sadness that we post the passing of Rose Royce original drummer, Henry passed away today and we are all in tears, RIP Henry you will be missed and never forgotten.” No cause of death was given.

Born October 16, 1954, in New Orleans, Louisiana, Garner moved to Los Angeles as a youngster and developed his skills as a drummer playing in the marching band at Washington High School. He went on to help found Rose Royce, the group behind some of the most enduring songs of the 1970s, including the No. 1 hit “Car Wash,” along with “I Wanna Get Next to You,” “I'm Going Down,” “Wishing on a Star” and “Love Don't Live Here Anymore.”

Garner kept time behind the band for decades, staying with Rose Royce through its run of soul classics and its years on the road, and he remained part of the group's story to the end.

Sources: Rose Royce official announcement; SoulTracks.
